title: Iron Bank Meter Station — external regulatory release-boundary challenge

source.binding_method: official FERC domain + docket identity + Environmental Assessment conditions + later official FERC record quoting the May 23, 2019 authorization and its stated evidentiary basis

historical_evidence_cutoff.basis: Evidence available before issuance of the May 23, 2019 Authorization to Commence Service.
historical_evidence_cutoff.rule: No hour-level cutoff is invented. Later descriptions of the authorization may corroborate what FERC says it relied upon but are not backfilled as contemporaneous evidence.

source_locators.location: A.1 Introduction / A.2 Purpose and Need
source_locators.fact: The project is the Iron Bank Meter Station Project in Docket CP18-499-000. FERC staff prepared the Environmental Assessment for use in the Commission's decision process concerning whether to authorize Rover's proposal.

Rover was required to file recurring status reports covering construction status, problems and noncompliance, corrective actions, complaints, and related regulatory correspondence until construction and restoration activities were complete.

Rover was required to receive written authorization from the Director of the Office of Energy Projects before placing the project into service; such authorization would be granted only after a determination that rehabilitation and restoration of affected areas were proceeding satisfactorily.

source_locators.location: footnote 52 quoting the May 23, 2019 CP18-499 authorization
source_locators.fact: FERC's later official record states that the May 23, 2019 authorization was granted on the basis of Commission staff's April 1, 2019 field inspection and Rover's May 21, 2019 construction status report, which included photographic evidence and reported progress for restoration activities.

contemporaneous_evidence_and_observation: Commission staff field inspection dated April 1, 2019, as identified by FERC's later official record.
Rover construction status report dated May 21, 2019, as identified by FERC's later official record.
Photographic evidence included with the May 21 status report, as described by FERC.
Reported progress for restoration activities, as described by FERC.
contemporaneous_known_requirements_and_c: Written OEP authorization was required before the project could be placed into service.
The stated predicate for that authorization was a determination that rehabilitation and restoration of the right-of-way and other project-affected areas were proceeding satisfactorily.
Recurring construction/restoration status reporting was part of the environmental compliance control structure.

human_or_regulatory_decision.decision_source_status: confirmed by later official FERC record quoting the original authorization
human_or_regulatory_decision.effect: permission to cross the FERC in-service authorization boundary under the cited environmental condition

subsequent_operational_state.note: The selected sources establish the authorization boundary and its issuance, not the exact later physical service-transition timestamp.

gap_assessment.diagnostic_observation: The record exposes an evidence-to-authority-to-permission relationship that may be relevant to future cross-domain extension design if the same requirement recurs in qualifying operational workflows.

non_claims: PayGod does not substitute for FERC, issue federal authorizations, or prove legal compliance.
The selected FERC materials do not establish the frozen Gas Site Readiness pressure, valve, fire-protection, leak-detection, notification, or warning-sign booleans.
The May 23, 2019 authorization is not treated as proof of complete mechanical or physical readiness.
The later FERC record is used to identify FERC's stated evidentiary basis for the 2019 authorization; it is not silently treated as a contemporaneous 2019 artifact.
No decision-authority primitive, release primitive, Pack change, or kernel change is authorized by this challenge.
